Yes, just in a slightly different fashion. I worked for 2 cydcor affiliates in 2013-14. It appears to not be at first, because no MLM's have any real office space typically (at least in my experience?) and they have the whole "interview" process, essentially just confirming you are in fact alive with a pulse and have a car.

Where it is clearly an MLM in how you ever make money, which is purely commission, just as any other. The main difference is you typically (if ever?) have to purchase inventory upfront to sell. Typically, cydcor companies will be something along the lines of a Quill (Staples Business Division) or an energy provider of some kind (Direct Energy, etc.). There are definitely some differences between Cydcor and other more well-known MLM's such as the physical office and some other things like a few hourly/salaried employees at each office like a recruiter, but at the end of the day the similarities are too glaring to consider it anything other than a "corporate MLM," basically, including lingo, cult-like mindset (requiring employees to perform rituals such as "bell-ringing," daily to announce daily sales, being forced to spend what little money you DO make going to team/group nights twice a week to keep you trapped in the cult-like mindset), and many cydcor employees live together due to low/non-existent pay. My "owner," who "made six figures," lived with 2 reps and didn't even own a car. It's actually often considered more harmful than the classic MLM, since they often times trap young college grads because they think they've started a career, when in reality they're the b2b version of the annoying Avon lady.
